A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPG research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–J are available and matchable, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original CPG benchmark experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, and robustness analyses, including additional image and audio evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices, including classification scores, pseudo-label analyses, and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same filtering and voting mechanisms, iterative labeled-set construction, logit adjustment, class-aware augmentation, auxiliary branch, losses, and prediction procedure. Figure 2's restyling does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10-LT, CIFAR-100-LT, Food-101-LT, and SVHN-LT, plus ESC-50-LT and ImageNet-127 in Appendix E. The same distribution-mismatch, noisy-label, and extreme-data scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain FixMatch, FreeMatch, SoftMatch, ACR without anchor distributions, SimPro, CDMAD, and supervised references. Appendix comparisons also retain ACR with anchors and the auxiliary-branch variants of FreeMatch and SimPro. The edited baseline paragraph changes no comparator membership.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, sample counts, imbalance ratios, preprocessing, architectures, resolutions, training budgets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Table 11's B1-to-B heading correction refers to the same extreme-imbalance setting already defined in Appendix E.5.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the component ablation, pseudo-label evolution analysis, imbalance and noise robustness tests, extreme-setting and architecture checks, and confidence-threshold, auxiliary-branch, and anchor-distribution analyses in Section 4.3 and Appendices A, E, and F.

E5.justification: Appendix D still specifies three random seeds, 0, 1, and 2, with mean and standard deviation reporting. Section 4.3 and Table 6 retain the same pairwise t-tests at the 0.05 significance level.

E6.justification: Reported scores, uncertainty values, significance counts, rankings, and empirical plots are unchanged throughout Tables 1–16 and Figures 1 and 3–7. For example, Table 11 retains CPG accuracies of 69.56, 49.28, and 77.78; only its final column heading changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, losses, Theorem 1, assumptions, and Appendix B's lemmas and proof are unchanged. Reflowing the problem-formulation paragraph changes no mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and scope: handling unknown arbitrary unlabeled distributions through CPG, a conditional generalization-error argument, minority-class augmentation, and an auxiliary branch. The reported maximum 15.97-point accuracy advantage is unchanged.

C2.justification: Explanations of pseudo-label reliability, distribution approximation, component effects, and smaller CIFAR-100-LT gains are retained. Appendix H preserves the same limitations concerning noisy labeled data and extremely limited supervision with uniformly distributed labeled data.

D1.justification: Appendices C, D, and I retain the same dataset preparation, hyperparameters, optimizer, software, hardware, and computing-time information. The code-access statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 52 works are cited, and Section 2 and Appendix G retain the same research positioning. Added AAAI abbreviations and page numbers for reference 34 are bibliographic updates, not new citations or positioning changes.

P1.justification: The baseline paragraph receives small wording edits, including replacing 'i.e.' with 'including' and removing 'recent.' Bibliographic details and the version/date stamp are updated, with limited text reflow and no section reorganization.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes typography, hatching, shading, and spacing while depicting the same optimization cycle. Table 11 changes 'Setting B1' to 'Setting B' and slightly adjusts column spacing. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v6 provides local editorial polish through Figure 2 restyling, reference updates, and correction of Table 11's heading. The corresponding setting was already clearly defined in v1, and the methods, empirical support, proofs, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged. These small presentation edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
